summary.headline: NCC Q1 FY27 consolidated turnover rose 12% to INR 5,842 crore with EBITDA margin of 9.38%; FY27 guidance issued (8-10% revenue growth, 8.5-9% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated turnover grew 12% YoY to INR 5,842 crore, the highest Q1 and overall consolidated turnover in company history, while standalone turnover rose 12% to INR 4,952 crore. Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.38% from 8.81%, but PAT margin was 3.7% and consolidated PAT fell to INR 216.4 crore from INR 192.1 crore only on a reported basis (standalone PAT fell 1.4% YoY). Order book closed at INR 81,214 crore after INR 3,889 crore of inflows in the quarter, and management issued its first FY27 guidance. Debt rose sharply, with consolidated net debt at INR 3,513 crore, driven by smart-meter project loans.

segments.name: Order book by division
segments.commentary: Buildings INR 22,357 crore (28%), Transportation INR 16,344 crore (20%), Electrical T&D INR 13,312 crore (16%), Mining INR 13,400 crore (16%), Water & Railways INR 10,994 crore (14%), Irrigation INR 4,806 crore (6%). Subsidiaries hold INR 9,902 crore of the total; standalone INR 71,312 crore.

segments.name: BharatNet (OFC)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR 185 crore and cumulative about INR 620 crore; balance order about INR 6,500 crore on a fixed-price contract, with optical fibre cable prices rising.

segments.name: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)
segments.commentary: Total JJM order book INR 5,881 crore (groundwater INR 3,524 crore, surface water INR 2,358 crore). Collections of INR 610 crore in Q1 against INR 2,771 crore UBR, with INR 413 crore more received in July; UP outstanding INR 1,043 crore.

segments.name: Ken-Betwa (river linking)
segments.commentary: Total contract value INR 3,390 crore with about INR 116 crore executed so far; site fully mobilised with equipment received.

segments.name: Smart meters (NCC Quantum Technologies)
segments.commentary: Holding company for two Maharashtra SPVs and one Bihar project; about 45% of an estimated 7-8 million meters installed; cumulative smart-meter debt INR 1,461 crore; capex to finish by March 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow guidance INR 22,000-25,000 crore.
Capex for FY27 maintained at INR 500 crore.
Standalone debt at March 2027 expected to be roughly flat YoY near INR 2,250-2,400 crore, depending on collections.
Orders booked in Q1 (INR 3,889 crore) expected to contribute turnover from Q3 FY27 onward.
Vizag Urban receivables of INR 271 crore expected by December 2026; AP Capital City old-project receivables of INR 142 crore expected this or early next quarter.
Smart-meter projects expected to finish capex by March 2027, after which O&M revenue accrues at about INR 1 crore per one lakh meters commissioned; TBM depreciation to start from Q3 FY27.
Management declined to give FY28 guidance or multi-year debt outlook.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex INR 170 crore against INR 500 crore FY27 budget.
Ken-Betwa site fully mobilised; monsoon may slow progress.
Smart meters: about 45% of 7-8 million meters installed (Maharashtra above 50%, Bihar lower); about INR 460 crore equity invested with no further equity needed.
TBM (tunnel boring machine) expected to start functioning, with depreciation rising from Q3 FY27.
Management said it has mobilised resources to complete smart-meter projects by March 2027.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow INR 3,889 crore, mainly Buildings and Water & Railways; July inflow took total to INR 4,542 crore. Book-to-bill about 3.5x.
Prospective bid pipeline about INR 2.5 lakh crore, not revised quarterly.
Client mix of order book: central govt about 14%, state govt about 19%, PSUs and state entities about 60%, multilateral banks about 5%, private about 4%.
Management said all INR 81,000 crore of the order book is executable, with slow-moving orders removed.
Commodities: steel and cement prices stable, but petroleum-linked items, aluminium, copper and OFC cable rising; about 81% of contracts have price escalation clauses that partly offset increases.
Payment cycles described as improving overall but varying by state and project.
Finance cost guided at around 3% of revenue; mobilisation advances INR 3,163 crore, 60% interest-bearing at 9.1%.
